items.title: 2026 Digital Kitchener Review - Final Report, COR-2026-102
notes:
The Committee considered Corporate Services Department report COR‑2026‑102, dated February 20, 2026, recommending approval of the Digital Kitchener Strategy, attached as Appendix 'A' to the report. The report further recommended that staff be directed to use the refreshed strategy to guide the City’s digital initiatives, priorities, and investments from 2026 to 2030.

N. Amaral, Innovation Lab Director, presented the report and responded to questions from the Committee. D. Chapman, Chief Administrative Officer, and D. Murray, Director of Technology Innovation and Services, were also in attendance to respond to questions.

In response to questions regarding implementation, N. Amaral provided an overview of Pitch Kitchener and its role in reviewing potential technology enhancements, including possible pilot programs. She also outlined both formal and informal opportunities for Council engagement throughout the year, noting that staff anticipate providing an annual formal update on the status of the strategy, supplemented by in‑person check‑ins with Council where feasible. In response to questions about communication from the Digital Innovation Lab, N. Amaral acknowledged this as an area for improvement and noted that initiatives are underway to enhance information sharing.

Committee members raised questions regarding digital literacy and access for individuals who may not have technology available to them. N. Amaral noted that service areas are being encouraged to consider the needs of their residents to ensure service interactions remain accessible and responsive.

D. Murray responded to additional questions regarding computer stations located in the City’s Community Centres, including educational opportunities available to users and the cybersecurity measures in place to support resident awareness of technology safety.

Mayor B. Vrbanovic entered the meeting at this time.

Councillor P. Singh noted his intention to bring forward an amendment related to expanding the computer refurbishment program delivered in partnership with the Working Centre.

Mayor B. Vrbanovic advised that such an amendment should be addressed separately, as it was not germane to the approval of the Digital Kitchener Strategy.

Councillor P. Singh agreed and indicated he would likely bring forward a notice of motion at the March 23, 2026 Council meeting.

Councillor A. Owodunni left the meeting at this time.
